description: CrackForest is an annotated road-surface image collection released for pavement distress detection. Cui and collaborators describe it as a database of urban road cracks and cite their random-forest detection studies. GitHub publishes JPEG image paths with MATLAB ground-truth and SEG annotation files; the complete tree lists 118 files in each annotation directory and more image files than annotation files. Coverage is road-surface photographs, but the README does not state the city, acquisition dates, image dimensions or a sampling frame. Version 1.0 is dated 29 September 2015. Access is free for noncommercial research under the provider’s stated restriction. A limitation is the mismatch between image and annotation counts, so the labelled subset must be identified before evaluation. Simulation uses include testing crack-detection uncertainty in road-condition observation models, without inferring structural capacity directly from a crack image. It complements data-nasa-prognostics-data-repository with infrastructure-surface evidence. No photograph, annotation array or archive was downloaded.
